abstract.reader_question: How can parallel verification accelerate generation without changing its distribution?
abstract.expected_relation: Draft proposals allow several tokens per target iteration, while accept-reject correction preserves sampling from the target distribution.

abstract.reader_question: When does the latency argument apply, and what was actually timed?
abstract.expected_relation: The predicted benefit depends on draft agreement, draft cost and spare compute; measured T5 latency is narrower evidence than acceptance measurements on other models.

methods.reader_question: What links exact sampling to the speed model?
methods.expected_relation: Probability correction preserves the target law, while proposal acceptance and relative draft cost determine expected tokens and walltime per iteration.

methods.reader_question: How do the timing trials differ from the wider model survey?
methods.expected_relation: Batch-one T5 trials on a single TPU-v4 measure walltime; the wider model survey estimates acceptance from target-generated tokens instead of measuring deployed speed.

results.reader_question: Why might proposal agreement and latency gains vary differently?
results.expected_relation: Acceptance must be interpreted together with draft-model cost and guess count; greater agreement alone does not determine the walltime gain.

results.reader_question: Which findings are measured speedups rather than projected opportunities?
results.expected_relation: Keep timed T5 results distinct from other models' acceptance estimates and negligible-cost projections, with sampling filters and compute limits qualifying the evidence.
